items.headline: Nasdaq falls about 5.5% into correction in worst day since April 2025
items.note: CNBC's live blog put the S&P 500 down about 4.4% and the Dow down roughly 1,800 points (3.4%); all 11 S&P sectors fell. CNBC's own pages gave conflicting figures for the S&P and Dow, so treat those as approximate. The cause was fear that AI infrastructure spending will slow after the midterms.

items.headline: Magnificent 7 lose more than $1 trillion as AI stocks get hit hardest
items.note: Nvidia fell more than 9% and AMD and Micron fell double digits on worries about data-center rules and high rates. The AI buildout funds many ML jobs and projects, so a slowdown would matter for your internship market.

items.headline: Qualcomm's weak outlook adds to the chip rout; memory shortage in focus
items.note: Qualcomm fell more than 9% after a disappointing quarterly outlook. CEO Cristiano Amon said, 'We don't have a demand issue; it's a supply issue,' pointing to industry memory shortages that raise prices.

items.headline: Asian chip stocks tumble; Korea's Kospi has a circuit-breaker day
items.note: The Nasdaq sell-off hit SK Hynix, Samsung, SoftBank and TSMC. CNBC reported the Kospi fell more than 6% at the close, after early losses large enough to trigger circuit breakers, and Japan's Nikkei and Taiwan's Taiex entered bear markets.

items.headline: Markets price about 70% odds of a Fed rate hike on Dec. 9
items.note: With oil near $100 (Brent) and rising rates already pressuring tech valuations, a hike is the market's base case. Higher rates make future profits of growth companies worth less today.

items.headline: October jobs report due Friday; about 59,000 jobs expected
items.note: Economists expect unemployment to hold at 4.2%. A weak or strong number could move rate-hike odds, which in turn moves the tech stocks that hire data and ML people.

items.headline: Jim Cramer: no AI stock seems safe as data-center uncertainty spreads
items.note: Commentary on why even strong AI names sold off together. It's an opinion piece, but it captures how much of the market now rides on one theme.

items.headline: Texas governor-elect wants to pause data-center expansion
items.note: Per CNBC, Gina Hinojosa said she wants a pause until protections are in place. Texas is a major data-center hub, so this is part of what spooked AI investors.

learn.explain: A circuit breaker is an automatic pause in trading when prices fall too fast, giving investors time to calm down and think. Exchanges set thresholds, such as a drop of a certain percent in one day. This week CNBC reported that South Korea's Kospi dropped enough early on to trigger its circuit breakers before closing down more than 6%. They don't stop a decline, they just slow panic selling.
learn.try: Look up the U.S. market-wide circuit breaker levels and compare them with this week's moves.
